text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.7% today and has dropped 7.5% over the past two weeks, a decline that tracks closely with crude oil prices sliding from recent highs. US oil fell to $89.62 per barrel today—down from peaks near $100 just days ago—and that matters for a refiner because lower crude costs reduce the value of refined products they sell; refineries are running at 95.2% capacity, so they're at full throttle but lack pricing power when input costs drop faster than output prices can follow.

The broader headwind is straightforward: crude prices are softening in a market watching geopolitical risk ease. Last week brought escalating Iran-US military tensions that had supported oil prices, but that fear premium appears to be fading as markets price in lower probability of imminent disruption to oil supplies. For a company whose profit margins depend on the spread between crude input and gasoline/diesel output, a falling oil price environment is a structural drag until crude stabilizes.
